info.title: Zega Cloud API
info.summary: Manage Zega Cloud projects, graphs, buckets and functions with an API token.
info.description:
The public management API of Zega Cloud: everything the dashboard does with projects, graphs, storage buckets and functions
except the things that change what you are billed, for the `zega cloud` command-line tool, Zega Studio and your own scripts.
It is a separate surface from the dashboard's API: same routes and answers, different credential.

## Authentication

`Authorization: Bearer zc_…`, an **API token** made in the dashboard (https://dashboard.zega.dev). The secret is shown once, when
the token is made. Nothing else is accepted: no cookie, no dashboard session, no graph key (`zk_…`) and no storage key
(`zs_…`), each of which opens its own resource's address instead. There are no CORS headers: this is not a browser API.
`GET /v1/whoami` says which token you are using.

## Scopes

- `read`: every GET. The default.
- `manage`: also everything that creates, renames, deletes or deploys: projects, graphs, buckets, functions, keys, variables, secrets, domains and the logs setting.

Each operation's `x-zega-scope` is the scope it needs. A `read` token calling a `manage` route gets 403 `scope_required`.

## What a token can never do

Everything about money is done in the dashboard, signed in: setting a spending cap (graph, bucket or function), starting a Checkout
(creating a graph, and so a project, which starts with one), resizing a graph, restoring a backup (it creates a billed volume).
Those answer 403 `session_required`. A token also cannot create, list or revoke tokens. They are listed under `x-session-only`.

## Restricting a token to one project

A token may be made for a single project. It then behaves as if the account owned only that project: its resources are visible, every
other project's graphs, buckets and functions are 404, the account-wide listings (`/v1/projects`, `/v1/graphs`, `/v1/buckets`,
`/v1/functions`, `/v1/usage`) show only that project, and a project cannot be created.

## Storage objects

A bucket's objects are not read or written through this API. The bucket's `url` is its own address, `https://<bucket-id>.zegadb.com`,
opened with a storage key (`zs_…`, made with `POST /v1/buckets/{bucket}/keys`): `PUT/GET/HEAD/DELETE /<key>` and `GET /?prefix=`.
Graph queries are the same: a graph's `hostUrl` with a graph key (`zk_…`).

## Limits and errors

Each token may make 300 requests every 60 seconds; past that, 429 with `Retry-After`. An account has at most
50 live tokens, each optionally expiring in 1 to 365 days.
Every error is JSON, `{"ok": false, "code": "<stable code>", "error": "<sentence>"}`: branch on `code`, show `error`. `x-error-codes` lists every code with its status.
Each operation's `x-error-codes` lists the codes it can give.

missing_token.meaning: No `Authorization: Bearer zc_…` header. Cookies and dashboard sessions are not accepted.

invalid_token.meaning: The token is not valid: mistyped, never made, or not an API token.

wrong_credential.meaning: A graph key (`zk_…`) or a storage key (`zs_…`) was sent. They open their own resource's address, not this API.

token_revoked.meaning: The token was revoked in the dashboard.

rate_limited.meaning: The token made more than 300 requests in 60 seconds, or too many bad credentials came from this address. `retryAfterSeconds` and the `Retry-After` header say how long to wait.

scope_required.meaning: The token's scope is `read` and the route changes something. Make a `manage` token.

session_required.meaning: Never available to a token: everything about money (spending caps, Checkout, resizing) and the token routes. It is done in the dashboard.

project_restricted.meaning: The token is restricted to one project and the route is account-wide with no per-project answer.

not_on_staging.meaning: Staging has one graph, one bucket and one function: creating, deleting and resizing are switched off there. Not given in production.

https_required.meaning: The API is served over https only.

not_found.meaning: No such route, or nothing at that path.

method_not_allowed.meaning: The route exists with other methods; or an `OPTIONS` (this is not a browser API: no CORS).

project_not_found.meaning: No such project of this account (or, for a restricted token, not the token's project).

graph_not_found.meaning: No such graph of this account (or not in the token's project).

bucket_not_found.meaning: No such bucket of this account (or not in the token's project).

function_not_found.meaning: No such function of this account (or not in the token's project).

key_not_found.meaning: Not an active key of this graph or bucket.

domain_not_found.meaning: Not a domain of this graph.

bad_name.meaning: A name is 1 to 64 characters (a variable or secret name: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit).

value_too_long.meaning: A value is at most 5,120 characters.

bad_code.meaning: A function is one JavaScript module with `export default { fetch(request, env) { … } }`.

code_rejected.meaning: The platform refused the module; the error says why. Nothing changed.

code_too_large.meaning: A function is one module of at most 1,000,000 bytes: bundle it first.

bad_logs_query.meaning: A log query parameter is out of range (`from`, `to`, `limit`, `status`, `q`, `cursor`).

bad_filter.meaning: A request-log filter is not valid.

bad_hostname.meaning: Not a domain you can add (zega.dev and zegadb.com names cannot be).

graph_busy.meaning: A graph changed while the project was being deleted. Try again.

last_graph.meaning: The only graph in its project: delete the project instead.

graph_not_running.meaning: Only a paid, running graph can have domains.

no_paid_graph.meaning: Storage is bought with a graph: the project has none that is paid and running.

bucket_limit.meaning: A project holds at most 10 buckets.

bucket_not_empty.meaning: The bucket still holds objects. Delete them at its own address, or delete the project.

function_limit.meaning: A project has at most 50 functions.

name_in_use.meaning: The name is already used by a variable or a secret of this function.

too_many_settings.meaning: A function has at most 64 variables and secrets.

not_deployed.meaning: Deploy the function's code first: a secret is set on the deployed script.

domain_taken.meaning: The domain is connected to a graph already.

domain_exists.meaning: The domain is already on this graph.

domain_limit.meaning: A graph has at most 3 domains.

domain_account_limit.meaning: An account has at most 10 domains across its graphs.

apply_failed.meaning: Saved, but the function's code was refused with these settings; the message says why.

domain_failed.meaning: The certificate provider did not accept the change.

monitoring_unavailable.meaning: Monitoring cannot be read right now. The graph is not affected.

service_misconfigured.meaning: A problem on our side; we have been notified. `effect` says whether anything changed.

busy_try_again.meaning: Zega Cloud is handling a lot of requests: wait `retryAfterSeconds`. `effect` says whether anything changed.

temporarily_unavailable.meaning: Zega Cloud could not complete this just now: wait `retryAfterSeconds`. `effect` says whether anything changed; a call that may have gone through is safe to repeat.

domains_unavailable.meaning: Custom domains are not available on this deployment.
